courseTitle: NativeScript + Angular: Build Native iOS, Android & Web Apps

cues.en: So that is the end of this module.
Again, we went through a lot of steps to implement authentication here because we don't just have simple
authentication where you can sign up and login.
Instead, we manage automatic login to check whether there is a stored token, a stored user data piece
in our local device storage, and we do store data there in the first place.
We got all the log out to set a timer and log a user out.
We have a guard in place to handle our redirection when the app starts and to ensure that we forward
the user to the to the right path and our app.
And with all of that, we have a solid setup that you should be able to use in your apps, even if you're
Because in the end, besides that rule thing here, which we played around with in the end, besides
that, we communicated with Firebase through its off rest API.
So that is totally something you can use with your own API to just as long as it returns a token.
But tokens are the defacto standard for authenticating users in mobile apps because you can't manage
a session there, you have no ongoing connection to your back backend.
You don't get views rendered by your back and you only exchange data and therefore you typically use
Just as I showed it to you in this module.
